eclss.reconciliation: Phase III wrote "a 2-3 t premium" for the modular option; its own table gave 9.6 t for 5 units (8 extra person-capacities x 1.2 t). The premium of the modular approach over two 6-person strings is the extra capacity, 1.2 t per 4-person unit beyond the three that 12 people need.
eclss.finding: Five units (3 + 2) carry 12 in ring A but not after the loss of ring A (8 capacity in B). Six units (3 + 3) survive a ring loss but not a ring loss plus one failed unit. Seven units with one cross-ring unit in the hub, or eight (4 + 4), close every case: 12 in one ring after a ring loss and a unit failure. Nominal aggregate capacity is not emergency availability. Recommended: 7 units (8.4 t nominal, +4.8 t over two 6-person strings).

transport.finding: The OPEN hot-loop pumps are derived: an existing-type pumped Li loop (H1, dT 200 K) needs ~12-34 MW of pump work and carries ~470-700 t of lithium in its trunks and channels, which no mass line holds today. Raising dT to 400 K and tapering the headers (H2) cuts that to ~5-15 MW and ~150-240 t. Long heat pipes fail on capillary limits: an Li fin across the blade carries its strip only to ~1.5 m, so passive transport is local. H3 (pumped trunk + short heat-pipe fins) and H5 (six independent zones) keep the pump work near 4-9 MW, cut the panel inventory, and turn a dust puncture from a loop loss into a fin or zone loss. H4 (vapour trunk) exploits the gravity-assisted return in every burn but cannot start frozen or run in 0 g. Recommended study basis: H5 with heat-pipe fins (H3 inside each zone).

thermal.finding: In a burn every radiator surface on a blade can see the 1800 K hot sections of the other two blades. The production design already answers this for WARM and LOW: its three-layer graded bulkhead (r 6.1-37 m) is a full annular baffle, and behind it WARM and LOW see the hot faces with F ~2-6e-4 (verified here): in a burn they absorb ~15-20 % of what they emit, a capacity debit the ledger does not yet carry (it worsens the LOW margin), not a failure. Without the bulkhead F would be 0.025 and 0.008 and neither could work. The Phase III 550 K section on the hot-blade forward end sits aft of that bulkhead and is fully exposed (F 0.02: it absorbs 2-3x what it emits), so option F as drawn has no sink in a burn. Moving the bulkhead aft of the new section (N2-R4a) restores the shadow (F < 1e-3) with no new element. A forward extension beyond LOW collides with the aft storage front at x 93.4.

l2.finding: Two units at EOL must carry 5.2 MW nominal (8.2 MW at the high band) once the OPEN planning loads, buffer recharge and standby are counted, so the continuous optimum rating is 3.12 MWe nominal and 4.93 MWe at the high band (2.30 / 3.48 MWe without the planning loads). 2.66 and 3.0 MWe fail after one loss at EOL; 3.5 MWe closes the nominal band with ~0.6 MW margin; no rating in the 2.66-4 MWe range closes the high band after a loss unless the planning loads are shed. Strategy C (three at 2/3 load) loses nothing at the moment of a trip; B needs ~1 h on one unit and costs ~3 % of a unit's heat in standby; A leaves 6-24 h on one unit. Recommended study basis: 3 x 3.5 MWe, strategy C, B as the maintenance mode, with high-band planning loads sheddable.

district.finding: Phase III placed the He-3 tanks 54 m from the district and outside the shadow cone; the tank farm is in fact forward of the radiator zone (ship x 109-138), ~195 m from the units and 9.0 deg off axis at most: inside the 12.5 deg shadow cone. With the transport-informed leakage (0.94 n per fission, surrogate core) and the S3 deposit (1.01 MeV in the He-3 per incident neutron, almost all at 3 K), one bare 3.5 MWe unit would put ~25.2 W into each tank at that distance; three units against a 25 % share of the 118 W lift (PROTOTYPE allocation) need a transmission of 0.11 (~17 cm of LiH), which the 244 cm shadow shield exceeds by many orders. The direct path closes. What stays OPEN is scatter: neutrons and gammas leaving the unshielded sides scatter off the blades, the casing and the tank farm structure toward the tanks; that needs the 3-D transport model (DR4-08). Gammas deposit mostly in the warm wall, not at 3 K.

container.structural: 6 t gross at 1.36 g peak axial = 80 kN per container on four twist-locks (rated 1.5 g: 88 kN)

logistics.finding: Counts follow mass (6 t gross, 1 t tare), not volume: dense loads (water, food) fill a container by mass at a third of its volume. Sharing containers between compatible categories (dry consumables A; frozen F; water W; medical M; spares S; reserve R; hazardous H always alone) saves ~20-35 % of containers against one category per container. Phase III counts omitted the tare: 1 t per container adds 10-20 t of departure mass.

missions.finding: With one hardware set (tanks sized once for 0.016 c), a slower mission carries the same tankage and its end mass changes only by its consumables. At 45 AU every speed fits in a few months and 0.004-0.008 c costs a third to a half of the propellant; at 120-200 AU 0.008 c keeps round trips near 1-1.5 years; from ~500 AU the 0.004 c case exceeds 36 months and higher speed pays most; at 1,000 AU only 0.012-0.016 c stay inside 36 months. The table gives days saved per 100 t of departure mass for each step; the owner sets the value of a day.

Keep the 12.5 deg shadow cone as the tank protection (tanks at ~200 m, <= 8 deg off axis) and carry a 0-10 t scatter allowance until 3-D transport

Adopt the independent restart pack (2-6 t) for R1b; study an APU as its alternative
Commission a 3-D OpenMC model of the district, blades and tank farm with the IV-B workflow (local or CI-side)
Choose how to value mission days against departure mass for the speed choice (IV-H)
